Jayakumar,

 W/o Shankarachari,
 Aged about 48 years.

 Doddabommasandra,
 Vidyaranyapura, Bengaluru.
 2 C.C.4972/2017  4. Anitha,
 W/o Shanugam,

 R/at No.178, Railway Station road,

1 Date of occurrence of offence Between 01.05.2015 and  11.11.2016 Date of report of offence 01.12.2016
Name of the Complainant Smt. Priya Date of Commencement of 07.10.2021 recording Evidence Date of Closing of Evidence 18.07.2024
Offences complained of U/s498(A), 504, 506 r/w 34  of I.P.C. and section -3 and 4  of Dowry Prohibition Act Opinion of the Judge Accused -1, 2 & 4 are  found not guilty.

This chargesheet is submitted by the Police Inspector of Vidyaranyapura Police Station against the accused persons for the offences punishable U/s498(A), 504, 506 r/w 34 of I.P.C. and Section- 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act  3 C.C.4972/2017  2.The

case of the prosecution is that, on 01.05.2015 the marriage of accused No.1 and CW.1 was held at Lakshmi Venkateshwara Kalyana Mantapa, Yashwanthpur, at the time of marriage 100 gram gold, Rs.50,000 cash was given to accused No.1 as dowry, after marriage she was well with accused and thereafter, the accused have started to give torture CW.1 physically and mentally saying that her parents have not done the marriage well, not given good gifts,
abused her in filthy language and ousted her from home by snatching her gold ornaments and gave life threat to bring more dowry from her parents house and thereby the accused have committed the offences punishable U/s.498A, 504, 506 r/w 34 of I.P.C. and Roopa vs Jayakumar on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31053440/
2 U/s. 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
 3.
The accused No.1, 2 and 4 are on bail.
Case against accused No.3 is abated as he dead.
As required  4 C.C.4972/2017 u/sec. 207 of Cr.PC, the copies of the charge sheet papers were furnished to the accused.

Charge was framed for the offences punishable U/s498(A), 504,
506 r/w 34 of I.P.C. and U/s 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and read over and explained to the accused in the language known to them.
Accused have pleaded not guilty and claimed for trial.

4. The prosecution, in order to prove its case,
has examined PWs.1 to 6 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 14.

On closure of the evidence on the side of the prosecution, the statement of the accused u/sec. 313 Cr.PC came to be recorded, the accused have denied the incriminating evidence appearing against them and chosen to lead defense evidence and as such accused No.1 himself examined as DW.1 and got marked Ex.D.1 to 11.
 5 C.C.4972/2017  5.
Heard the arguments.
Perused the documents placed on record.

Roopa vs Jayakumar on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31053440/
3  6.

The points that arise for consideration are :
 1. Whether the prosecution has proved  beyond all reasonable doubt that  accused have committed the offences  U/s.498(A), 504, 506 r/w 34 of I.P.C.
 and U/s. 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition  Act.?
 2. What order ?
 7. The above points are answered as under :
 Point No.1: In the Negative.

Point No.2: As per final order for the following :
 REASONS

8. Point No.1 : The case of the prosecution is that, accused have tortured CW.1 physically and mentally demanding more dowry from her parents home and abused her in filthy language and  6 C.C.4972/2017 threatened her life with dire consequences and thereby accused have committed offences aforesaid.

9. The Ld. Sr.APP for the state during the course of argument has submitted that prosecution has examined complainant, mahazar witnesses and police officials, the evidence placed by prosecution through prosecution witnesses and documentary evidence are clearly establishes that the accused have committed Roopa vs Jayakumar on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31053440/
4 the offense as alleged in the charge sheet.

Therefore,
prays to convict the accused by imposing maximum sentence.
10. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for accused has submitted written arguments.

In the written arguments, submitted that, after amrriage of accused No.1 and CW.1, CW.1 has not at all co- habited with accused No.1, she always used to stay with her parents house whenever she was called by her parents.

In the month of June 2015 CW.1 picked up quarrel with accused No.1 without any reason, in  7 C.C.4972/2017 this regard despite panchayath held on several time,
she did not turn up to lead matrimonial life.
Prosecution has examined 6 witnesses as PW.1 to PW.6, out of them, PW.1 is complainant, PW.2 mahazar witness and close relative of PW.1.
PW.3 is Investigating officer, PW.4 and PW.5 are father and mother of PW.1, PW.6 is sister of PW.1.

After marriage,
PW.1 led marital life with accused No.1 only 30 days as admitted by PW.1 herself.

The only reason beyond this case is, PW.1 wants to continue her education,
but it was not accepted by accused.
The evidence of PW.2 shows that one Rado watch, two severan chain and 8 gram gold was given to accused No.1 contrarily it was not stated by her in her statement before police.

Roopa vs Jayakumar on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31053440/
5
PW.5 is father of PW.1 has deposed same as of PW.2 regarding Rado watch, two severan gold chain and 8 gram gold given to accused No.1 but he has not stated by him in his statement before police.

PW.3 is an investigating officer who filed charge sheet after  8 C.C.4972/2017 completion of investigation without visiting house of PW.1 and made inquiry of PW.1's neighborer as deposed in his evidence.
Hence, the prosecution has failed to prove allegation made in the charge sheet.
Therefore, the accused is entitled to benefit of doubt and prays for acquit the accused.

11. In the light of the submission made above,
on careful perusal of oral and documentary evidence placed by the prosecution, no doubt, PW.4 and 5 are father and mother of PW.1, PW.6 is her sister, PW.2 is close relative of PW.1 and PW.3 is investigating officer

,
except evidence of relatives of PW.1, no evidence of independent witnesses is on record.
PW.1 in her cross examination has clearly deposed that she led matrimonial life with accused only 30 days that to she used to stay at her parental house during that time.

The allegation as to dowry is concerned, the case of the prosecution is 100 gram gold and Rs.50,000 cash was given to accused No.1 as dowry at the time of  9 C.C.4972/2017 Roopa vs Jayakumar on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31053440/
6 marriage.

In this regard, PW.1 has deposed that 100 Gram gold and Rs.50,000/- cash was given to accused No.1 at the time of marriage and she denied except one gold ring exchanged by each other, no such dowry was demanded by accused.
PW.4 mother of PW.1 deposed that gold ornaments of 100 gram was put to PW.1 and only Rs.50,000/- cash was given to accused No.1, but she does not know its denomination.
PW.5 father of PW.1 deposed supporting evidence of PW.4 regarding cash of Rs.50,000/- was given to accused No.1.

In order to prove oral testimony of said witnesses,
prosecution has not placed neither corroborative evidence of independent witness is on record nor any documentary evidence, in the absence of such cogent and reliable evidence, the evidence of daughter, father and mother is not safe to believe and does not inspire confidence.

12. Coming to another allegation of prosecution as to marriage exigences incurred by parent of PW.1,
 10 C.C.4972/2017 prosecution has relied on Ex.12 copy of receipt dated 10.04.2015 which shows Rs.36,000 was paid as fair to travel from Mysore to Bengalaur, it does not contain signature of author of said receipt and date of Roopa vs Jayakumar on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31053440/
7 departure is mentioned as 30.04.15 and 1.5.15.
Another cash bill dated 25.05.2015 Ex.P.13 shows Rs.40,000 paid, however, by going through Ex.P.12 and 13 it cannot be said that which relates to marriage expense incurred by PW.5.

Ex.P.14 is the bill of payment made to cook to prepare lunch for 800 members on 31.5.2015 and breakfast for 350 members on 1-6-2016, admittedly marriage was held on 01.05.2015, while comparing the date of marriage and date of order made for lunch and breakfast it would clearly shows that said order was not made for lunch and breakfast for marriage.

The accused has placed documents to show marriage exigences incurred by him which is marked as Ex.D.1 to Ex.D.7, they are the bills relating to amount paid towards list of grocery for  11 C.C.4972/2017 lunch, purchase grocery, decoration of marriage Hall,
amount paid to Kalyanamantapa for marriage ceremony.
In the cross examination accused has clearly deposed that those documents do not speaks about purchased grocery by him, decoration, catering for the purpose of marriage.

However, in view of above,
it can be said that oral and documentary evidence placed by the prosecution is not suffice to prove guilt of accused for alleged offence.

Roopa vs Jayakumar on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31053440/
8  13.

PW.3 is an investigating officer, in his cross examination has clearly deposed that he has not visited of house of PW.1 and not made any inquiry of neighbors as to alleged offence committed by accused as argued by the learned counsel for accused.
By this evidence of PW.3, one can be gather that prosecution has not been able to establish guilt of accused for alleged offence beyond reasonable doubt.
14. Therefore, in view of discussion made above, the considered opinion is of the court that, the prosecution
has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt
. The accused are entitled to benefit of doubt.
Hence, answered the point No.1 in the Negative.
15. Point No.2:

In view of discussion made on point No.1 this court proceeds to pass following  ORDER Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C the accused-1, 2 & 4 are acquitted of the offences punishable under sections punishable under sections - 498(A), 504, 506 r/w 34 of I.P.C. and Section - 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Bail bonds of accused-1, 2 & 4 and their surety bonds stand cancelled after six months from today.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcript computerized by her, revised, corrected and then pronounced by me in the open Court on this 3 rd day of February, 2025)

( PUTTARAJU ) VII Addl.
